replies.What is your relationship with mathemati: I never really liked math beyond what was needed for school. I remember struggling with algebra and geometry, especially when it came to remembering formulas. My parents both had lower secondary education, so they didn’t help much. I’ve kept up with basic arithmetic but don't use advanced math in my daily life as a self-employed photographer.
replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: Yes, I do feel some anxiety around math, especially if it's something new or complex. It’s not the kind of anxiety that paralyzes me, but it does make me hesitate to dive into problems without understanding them first. I tend to avoid anything too abstract or technical, which makes me nervous when I see equations with many variables.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: I used a simple calculator app on my phone for basic operations and once tried an online tool to solve quadratic equations. Then use the quadratic formula: x equals negative b plus or minus square root of b squared minus four ac all over two a. Plug in your values and calculate. You’ll get two solutions, which could be real numbers or complex ones depending on the discriminant.

Take the derivative of f(x), call it f'(x). Set f'(x) equal to zero and solve for x. These are your critical points. Then plug each value back into the original function to get the corresponding y-values. These (x,y) pairs are the stationary points, which could be maxima or minima.
